decision_question: Which YC small-team agent companies show the clearest commercially viable use cases?
headline: Workflow-heavy, operator-owned agent products are the clearest commercial pattern in the Spring 2025 YC cohort.

findings.title: Workflow automation leads the cohort
findings.statement: The highest-signal YC agent companies are wrapped around concrete operational jobs, not generic assistant positioning.
findings.implication: The strongest wedge is workflow ownership with a clear operator and measurable queue.
findings.metric: 8 companies in the workflow automation cluster

findings.title: Operational categories dominate broad agent narratives
findings.statement: Customer ops, analytics, QA, testing, and infrastructure appear more frequently than generic platform claims.
findings.implication: Buyers respond better to operational jobs and embedded tooling than to abstract agent platform language.
findings.metric: Top clusters: workflow automation, sales and customer ops, analytics and reporting, developer tools and testing

findings.title: The cohort is very early but already shaped
findings.statement: Most of the filtered Spring 2025 companies are tiny teams, yet the use-case pattern is already visible.
findings.implication: The category signal is useful, but product and positioning are still converging.
findings.metric: Median team size 3; 13 teams have 1-2 people

findings.title: Healthcare operations is a credible vertical wedge
findings.statement: Healthcare admin workflows show enough density and pain to support focused product bets despite a smaller company count.
findings.implication: Vertical agents with painful, repetitive workflows can outrun broader horizontal positioning.

use_case_clusters.name: workflow automation
use_case_clusters.buyer: COO, operations leader, or workflow owner
use_case_clusters.workflow_owner: ops managers running repetitive multi-step work
use_case_clusters.business_job: Turn high-volume, rules-heavy operational queues into agent-run systems of action.
use_case_clusters.value_prop: Throughput, faster cycle times, and lower labor cost without requiring users to learn a new interface.
use_case_clusters.why_now: LLMs plus tool use make it possible to automate the whole queue, not just summarize it.
use_case_clusters.recommendation: Best starting point when a team already exists and the handoffs are obvious.

risks: YC directory and company website language can overstate product maturity.
Use-case labels are inferred from company text, not official taxonomy.
Only a subset of companies has deeper website-backed source notes; the rest fall back to directory evidence.

recommendations.title: Choose workflow-heavy use cases first
recommendations.why: 8 companies cluster around operational systems of action, making this the clearest YC pattern.

recommendations.title: Own context, governance, or workflow position
recommendations.why: The more durable clusters pair agents with data access, infrastructure, or embedded workflow ownership.

recommendations.title: Treat healthcare operations as a real wedge
recommendations.why: The count is smaller than horizontal ops, but the workflow pain and willingness to pay are strong.

recommendations.title: Avoid generic agent-platform messaging
recommendations.why: The cohort repeatedly rewards products with explicit jobs and operators, not broad agent claims.

chart_briefs.title: Use-case map by business shape
chart_briefs.why_this_fits: The question is strategic positioning, not exact counts.
chart_briefs.narrative_takeaway: The strongest names cluster where workflow ownership and willingness to pay are both high.
chart_briefs.encoding_guidance: Axes: horizontal = horizontal tooling to vertical workflow ownership; vertical = weak to strong willingness to pay.

methodology.approach: Discover the live YC companies backend, filter Spring 2025 agent-pattern companies with team size <= 10, summarize use-case clusters, and enrich representative names with website-backed proof lines.
limitations: This is a public-web analysis, not a financial or customer-validated market study.
Representative source coverage is deeper for highlighted names than for the full cohort.
The cohort snapshot can change as YC company pages or descriptions change over time.
